principle_text: When the persuadee provides neutral or factual responses that do not deepen emotional engagement, avoid relying solely on generic compliments or assumptions about their experiences.
When the persuadee introduces a new, serious concern unrelated to the donation topic, avoid continuing with unrelated small talk that does not connect to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shares personal concerns unrelated to the charity, avoid shifting focus away from the donation goal without linking their concerns back to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shares personal experiences unrelated to the donation goal, avoid responding with neutral or unrelated comments that do not connect back to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee references past charitable actions without expressing current interest, avoid assuming immediate willingness to donate again without further engagement.

When the persuadee expresses financial constraints and competing obligations, avoid emphasizing donation opportunities without acknowledging their current limitations or offering alternative ways to contribute.
When the persuadee expresses financial constraints but shows willingness to contribute, you should offer to match their donation to encourage even small contributions.
